priorities.name: Quiet, private space for calls and meetings
priorities.issue: Noise from meetings and calls on the open floor is the site's most negative theme, and phone-booth/private space is limited.
whatItLooksLike: distractions and noise level from people talking in meetings (unavoidable)
Temperature and limited number of phone booth/private workspaces

evidence.text: Noise & Distraction: 97 people (21% of respondents), 125 comments, 79% negative — the 2nd most-negative theme at the site (after Lighting).
Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (88/100); focused-work friction 28/100 (53% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Assess phone-booth/private-space capacity and a call-etiquette norm against demand before adding enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Measure booth demand vs. availability, pilot a call-etiquette norm, and size any gap for Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: Desk availability and sit/stand + workstation setup
priorities.issue: Associates want more offices and sit/stand desks, and dual monitors aren't reliably plug-and-play.
whatItLooksLike: Not enough offices, need more stand/sit desks.
Dual monitors sometimes dont work. it is not easy as plug and play. we have to spend time on it sometimes.

evidence.text: Physical Environment is the #2 priority category (79/100); Desk Availability: 75 people (17% of respondents), 92 comments, 57% negative.
Hardware: 104 people (23% of respondents), 150 comments, 58% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Review desk mix (offices, sit/stand) against demand and standardize workstation setup with routine checks.
priorities.siteMustDo: Quantify demand for offices/sit-stand seats and fix the dual-monitor setup reliability.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: Temperature is a frequent, specific complaint — the office runs cold and inconsistent — and it compounds the difficulty of focused work.
whatItLooksLike: Temperature (often too cold) recurs across comments; identify the specific zones and times during local validation.

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 77 people (17% of respondents), 93 comments, 73% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Have facilities check HVAC set-points and balancing in the affected zones and confirm whether it is a control, zoning, or equipment issue.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log the specific cold zones and times, submit to building operations, and verify the correction holds rather than assuming set-point changes stick.

priorities.name: On-site food and coffee
priorities.issue: The on-site market is thin and pricey for a site this size — especially mid-week — and coffee machines are often out of supplies or not working.
whatItLooksLike: The cafe at the Concourse is extremely bare and options available are not satisfactory. …
Market cafe item availability has become somewhat limited especially mid-week
The coffee machines seem to be out of supplies, non-functional, or having an issue more likely than I would expect. …

evidence.text: Food & Beverage: 97 people (21% of respondents), 122 comments, 44% negative — raised by 21% of respondents vs 19% company-wide; Cost / Pricing: 26 people (6% of respondents), 30 comments, 50% negative.
Availability of on-site food and beverage options: Under Supported — friction 19/100 (36% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Review the market's restock cadence, product range and pricing with Food & Beverage, and set a service standard for coffee-machine supplies and repairs.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log empty-shelf days and coffee-machine outages for four weeks and review them with the vendor against the new standard.

priorities.name: Restroom repairs and building upkeep
priorities.issue: Restroom fixtures — sinks, faucets, toilets — are frequently out of order and some areas are dusty, which associates notice on every visit.
whatItLooksLike: The ladies rooms are bad and have been for years. Some facets don't work, some toilets don't work and it often does not smell pleasant in there at all.
…4th floor restrooms generally have one sink working out of four
Annex building is dusty and upsets my allergies …

evidence.text: Reliability of building operations (elevators, restrooms): Under Supported — friction 13/100 (33% under-supported).
Cleanliness & upkeep: Under Supported — friction 12/100 (27% under-supported).
Cleanliness & Upkeep: 53 people (12% of respondents), 64 comments, 50% negative; Building Operations: 29 people (6% of respondents), 32 comments, 31% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Run a floor-by-floor restroom fixture audit, repair non-working sinks and toilets, and check cleaning frequency against current occupancy, including the Annex.
priorities.siteMustDo: Complete the fixture audit, track each repair to closure, and re-inspect in 30 days.
